retention.note: the per-job project copy is a regenerable input: the corpus is byte-identical for every job of a cell and is identified by its content hash. Observations, traces and per-parse evidence are kept.

session_full_publish.description: the project session with Spike 2 publication: every artifact is rewritten on every revision and CSS is re-aggregated from every contribution. The reference the other two are measured against.

session_incremental_publish.description: the project session publishing only the output delta: an artifact whose content digest matches the published one is reused rather than rewritten, and an artifact no longer claimed is removed. CSS is still aggregated in full, so this row isolates publication.

session_incremental_publish_css.description: the project session with delta publication AND incremental CSS aggregation: the stylesheet is re-derived from the changed rule contributions rather than from the whole atom population.

policy.engine_order_randomisation: per (cell, scenario, cache-state, iteration): the two engines are shuffled with a seed derived from the job identity, so thermal and order bias do not systematically favour one engine

timer.wall_clock_used_for: event ordering metadata only, never a duration

policy.os_cache_state_reason: dropping the OS page cache requires privileges this environment does not grant, and faking it with posix_fadvise would not reproduce a cold cache. Every number here is a WARM-OS-cache number and is labelled so.
